senses: That which causes shame; a disgrace, blot, blemish.
la:noun:dedecus.html:
dē-dĕcus, ŏris, n.,
disgrace, dishonor, infamy, shame (for syn. cf.: offensio, contumelia, infamia, ignominia, turpitudo, obscoenitas, injuria—freq. and class.).
In gen.: eos dolores atque carnificinas per dedecus atque maximam contumeliam te facere ausum esse? Cato ap. ; so with ignominia,; with infamia,; cf. ; with flagitium,; with probrum,: vitam per dedecus amittere,: in dedecora incurrunt,; cf. with damnum,: magnum fuit generi vestro,: dedecori est,: dedecori esse (alicui),; et saep.; cf. also: aliter ampla domus dedecori domino fit,.—
Concr. (as sometimes our word shame), that which causes shame; a disgrace, blot, blemish: cum nec prodere visum dedecus auderet (viz., the ass's ears of Midas), ; cf.: naturae dedecus, a monster, said of the ass, ; cf. ; . —
(Acc. to decus, no. II.) Like τὸ κακόν, moral dishonor, vice, turpitude; a vicious action, shameful deed, etc. (very freq.): decus, quod antiqui summum bonum esse dixerant ... itemque dedecus illi summum malum,; cf. ; : dedecus admittere,; ; ; : ad avertendos tantorum dedecorum rumores, et saep.; of unchastity, ; ; : dedecorum pretiosus emptor,: abdicamus occulta dedecoris,.

la:adj:dedecor.html:
dē-dĕcor, ŏris,
adj., unseemly, unbecoming, shameful, vile (rare): dedecorem amplexi vitam,: alga,: dedecores inultique caedebantur, (ap. P.).

la:adj:dedecorus.html:
dē-dĕcōrus, a, um,
adj., disgraceful, dishonorable, shameful (very rare), : majoribus suis,; .

la:verb:dedo.gloss: to hand over, surrender, give up, consign, deliver, yield, abandon
senses: to hand over, surrender, give up, consign, deliver, yield, abandon
la:verb:dedo.html:
dē-do, dĭdi, dĭtum (
infin. pass. parag.: dedier,), 3, v. a., lit., to give away, give up from one's self; hence, with respect to the term. ad quem, to give up any thing to one, to surrender, deliver, consign, yield (stronger than do, q. v.—freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: ancillas,; cf.: aliquem in pistrinum,: aliquem hostibus in cruciatum,; so, ad supplicium,: ad exitium,; : ad necem,; for which neci,; : telis militum,: aliquem istis,: mihi iratae infamem juvencum,,

46: Assyrios cineri odores,impart, devote,.—

Esp., milit. t. t., to deliver up, surrender some one or something to the enemy; and with se, to surrender one's self, capitulate: INIVSTE IMPIEQVE ILLOS HOMINES ILLASQVE RES DEDIER, an old formula in : urbem, agrum, aras, focos seque uti dederent,: eos, qui sibi Galliaeque bellum intulisset, sibi dedere,: so, auctores belli,: eum hostibus,: Cirtam,: Ambiani se suaque omnia sine mora dediderunt,: se suaque omnia Caesari,; : se alicui,; ; ; et saep.: se in ditionem atque in arbitratum Thebano poplo,; ; : incolumitatem deditis pollicebatur,; : se, without dat., ; et saep.
Trop.
In gen., to give up, yield, devote, dedicate; and with se, to give up, apply, devote, dedicate one's self (esp. freq. in Cic.): Davo ego istuc dedam jam negoti,: membra molli somno,: aures suas poetis,: animum sacris,: aliquem cupiditati crudelitatique alicujus,; so, filiam (Verginiam) libidini App. Claudii,; ef. : collegam liberto,: tuus sum, tibi dedo operam,; cf.: ubi ei dediderit operas, al.: corpora paupertate dedita morti,: se totum Catoni,; cf.: cui (sc. patriae) nos totos dedere ... debemus,; cf.: se toto animo huic discendi delectationi,: se penitus musicis,: se literis,: se ei studio,: se doctrinae,; ; : se amicitiae eorum,: ne me totum aegritudini dedam,; so, se totos libidinibus,; ; et saep.: cum se ad audiendum, legendum scribendumque dediderit,: dede neci,; ; : se ad literas memoriasque veteres,: cum se doctrinae penitus dedidissent,.—Absol.: dediderim periculis omnibus, ap. .—
dēdĭta ŏpĕra, adverb., purposely, designedly, intentionally, ; ; Afran. ap. ; ; ; ; ; in the order opera dedita,; and in MSS. ellipt., dedita,; cf. dedita, ἐπιτηδές, Gloss. —
In Partic.: manus, for the usual dare manus, to give up, to yield: si tibi vera videntur, dede manus; aut, si falsum est, accingere contra,.—Hence, dēdĭtus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to no. II. A.), given up to, addicted, devoted to something; eager, assiduous, diligent (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.).
With dat.: hoc magis sum Publio deditus, quod, etc.,; cf.: nimis equestri ordini deditus,: eorum voluntati et gratiae deditus fuit,: his studiis,; : studio literarum,: literis,: artibus,; cf. ; : nec studio citharae nec Musae deditus ulli,: animus libidini deditus,: vitiis flagitiisque omnibus,: ventri atque somno,; cf.: somno ciboque,: corporis gaudiis,; cf. : quaestui atque sumptui,; : agriculturae,: vino,.—Comp.: uxoribus deditior,.—Sup.: ab optimo certe animo ac deditissimo tibi, Dolab. ap. .—
In Lucret. and Catull. with in: in pugnae studio quod dedita mens est,: in rebus animus,; Catull. 61, 102.—*
With an adv. of place: ubi spectaculi tempus venit deditaeque eo (sc. ad spectacula) mentes cum oculis erant,.

la:verb:deduco.gloss: to lead or bring out or away, divert; escort, accompany, conduct (out of one's house as a mark of respect or for protection)
senses: to lead or bring out or away, divert; escort, accompany, conduct (out of one's house as a mark of respect or for protection)
to lead, fetch, bring or draw down; weigh down, outweigh
to stretch out, extend, draw out
to lead forth or conduct a colony to a certain place; found (a colony)
to bring to trial; bring before a tribunal as a witness
to withdraw, remove, draw off, lead off (troops from one place to another); conduct or bring to a place
to draw out a ship (from a port), launch
to draw a ship into port
la:verb:deduco.html:
dē-dūco, xi, ctum (
imper.: deduc,; old form, deduce,), 3, v. a., to lead or bring away, to lead, fetch, bring or draw down (for syn. cf.: duco, comitor, prosequor, persequor, stipo, sequor, consequor—freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.
Not designating a limit: atomos de via,to turn from a straight course,: eum concionari conantem de rostris,: pedes de lecto,: suos clam ex agris,; so, aliquem ex ultimis gentibus,: lunam e curru,; cf. the foll.: summā vestem deduxit ab orā,: cantando rigidas deducere montibus ornos,: lunam caelo ; cf.: lunam cursu,: hunc caelo,: dominam Ditis thalamo,: tota carbasa malo,i. e. to spread, unfurl, by letting down,; cf. the foll.: febres corpore,: inde boves,: transfuga duci se ad consules jubet deductusque traditurum urbem promittit,: Ubiis imperat, ut pecora deducant suaque omnia ex agris in oppida conferant,; cf. : rivos, i. e. to clear out, cleanse ( = detergere, ; ), Heyne ad loc.; cf.: aqua Albana deducta ad utilitatem agri suburbani,conducted off,, and v.the foll.: lunam,; cf. Jovem,the sun,: crines pectine,to comb,; cf.: caesariem barbae dextrā,: vela,: sive aliquis molli deducit candida gestu Brachia,moves, (3, 15), 5 (al. diducit); imitated by (al. diducit) et saep.—
Stating the limit: cito hunc deduc ad militem,: aliquem ad aliquem,; ; ; ; et saep.: juvenem ad altos currus,: suas vestes humero ad pectora,; cf.: manum ad imum ventrem, et saep.: impedimenta in proximum collem,: aquam in vias,; : aliquem in conspectum (Caesaris),: aliquem in arcem,; : aliquem in carcerem,: in arenam,: levis deducet pondere fratres, will bring down (the scale), . —
In partic.
Milit. t. t., to draw off, lead off, withdraw troops from a place; to lead, conduct, bring to a place: praesidia de locis, Sisenna ap. ; so with de, ; ; : exercitum ex his regionibus,; so with ex, fin.; 7, 81 fin.; : legionem ab opere,; so with ab, ; : deducta Orico legione,: exercitum finibus Attali,: deducto exercitu, ; ; ; cf. Oud. ad : milites ad Ciceronem,: tres in arcem cohortes praesidio,: a Flacco inter ceteros, quos virtutis causa secum ex provincia ad triumphum deducebat, deductus sum,: copias ex locis superioribus in campum deducit,: legionibus in hiberna deductis,; so, in hiberna,; : in interiorem Galliam,; cf. in Menapios,: in proxima municipia,: in hiberna in Sequanos,: in aciem,: praesidia eo,: neque more militari vigiliae deducebantur,; . —
Pub. law t. t., to lead forth, conduct a colony to a place: coloni, qui lege Julia Capuam deducti erant,; cf. : colonos in aliquem locum,: coloniam in aliquem locum,; ; ; ; (repeatedly); : Aquileia colonia Latina eo anno in agro Gallorum est deducta,; cf.: in colonia Capua deducti,: ut emantur agri a privatis, quo plebs publice deducatur,; cf. ; 2, 34, 92: triumvir coloniis deducendis,; cf. ; ; — Absol.: deductis olim et nobiscum per conubium sociatis, haec patria est,. —
Nautical t. t.
To draw out a ship from the docks: ex navalibus eorum unam (navem) deducit,: deducunt socii naves,.—Hence far more freq. meton., like the Gr. καθέλκειν, to draw down a ship from the stocks into the sea; to launch, ; ; : neque multum abesse (naves) ab eo, quin paucis diebus deduci possent,: naves,: classem,: naves litore,: carinas,; et saep.—
Rarely for subducere and the Gr. κατάγειν, to draw a ship into port: onerarias naves in portum deducunt,: in portum,.—
Weavers' t. t., to draw out, spin out the thread, yarn: dextera tum leviter deducens fila, Catull. 64, 313: filum,; ; .—Hence, meton., to prepare a web, to weave: vetus in tela deducitur argumentum,is interwoven, represented in weaving,.—
t. t. of common life, to lead out, conduct, escort, accompany a person out of the house, as a mark of respect or for protection: haec ipsa sunt honorabilia ... assurgi, deduci, reduci,: cum magna multitudo optimorum virorum et civium me de domo deduceret,; : ne deducendi sui causa populum de foro abduceret,; cf. : a quibus (sc. equitibus Rom.) si domus nostra celebratur, si interdum ad forum deducimur, etc.,.—
Esp., to conduct a young man to a public teacher: dicam hunc a patre continuo ad me esse deductum,; ; ; ; cf. ephebum in gymnasium, Petron. 85, 3.—
Aliquam alicui, ad aliquem, to lead, conduct a bride (from her father's house) to her husband (cf. denubo): bona uxor si ea deducta est usquam cuiquam gentium,; cf. Catull. 68, 143: virginem juveni marito,: uni nuptam, ad quem virgo deducta sit,: nullo exemplo deductae in domum patrui fratris filiae,; so, in domum,; so of the bridegroom himself, to take home the bride: domum in cubiculum,: uxorem domum,: quo primum virgo quaeque deducta est,fin.—Absol.: eas velut auspicibus nobilissimis populis deductas esse,; cf. .—
In a dishonorable sense, to bring one a concubine, ; ; ; ; ; cf. also the foll., no. 7.—
To lead about in a public procession, : invidens privata deduci superbo non humilis mulier triumpho,: tensas,; .—
Hence, to drive out, expel = expellere: Arsinoen ex regno, Auct. B.

Alex. 33: ex possessione,. —

Jurid. t. t.
Aliquem de fundo, to lead away a person from a disputed possession in the presence of witnesses (with or without force: the latter moribus, the former vi solida), in order to procure him the right of action (this was a symbolic procedure preparatory to an action): appellat Fabius, ut aut ipse Tullium deduceret aut ab eo deduceretur. Dicit deducturum se Tullius, etc., Cic. pro Tull. Fragm. § 20; ; placuit Caecinae constituere, quo die in rem praesentem veniretur, et de fundo Caecina moribus deduceretur, etc.,.—
To bring before a tribunal as a witness: multi boni ad hoc judicium deducti non sunt,.—
To bring to trial: lis ad forum deducta est,. —
With the accessory idea of diminution, to withdraw, deduct, subtract, diminish: cibum,. And as a mercantile t. t.: addendo deducendoque videre, quae reliqui summa fiat,: ut centum nummi deducerentur,; cf. : de capite deducite, quod usuris pernumeratum est,; cf. et saep.—Hence in a double sense: Tertia deducta est (in allusion to the meaning, no. 5, c. β), ; cf. the same account in .
Trop.
In gen., to bring down, bring or lead away, withdraw, bring, lead: quare, si placet, deduc orationem tuam de coelo ad haec citeriora, ap. , and 289, 9: licet enim contrahere universitatem generis humani, eamque gradatim ad pauciores, postremo deducere in singulos,: aliquem de animi lenitate,; cf.: aliquem de animi pravitate,: aliquem de sententia,: aliquem de fide, et saep.: perterritos a timore,: aliquem a tristitia, ab acerbitate,: aliquem ab humanitate, a pietate, a religione, (for which, shortly before, abducere): aliquem a vera accusatione,fin.; et saep.: voluntates impellere quo velit, unde autem velit deducere,: mos unde deductus,derived,; cf.: nomen ab Anco,: quae tandem ea est disciplina, ad quam me deducas,: aliquem ad fletum misericordiamque,: aliquem ad eam sententiam,; : rem ad arma,; cf.: rem ad otium,fin.: plura argumenta ad unum effectum, et saep.: quam in fortunam quamque in amplitudinem deduxisset (Aeduos),; so, aliquem in eum casum,: aliquem in periculum,: ; cf.: rem in summum periculum,; : rem in controversiam,: aliquem in causam,: in societatem belli, et saep.: huc jam deduxerat rem, ut, etc.,; so, rem huc, ut, etc.,: deduxisti totam hanc rem in duo genera solum causarum, caetera innumerabilia exercitationi reliquisti,have brought, reduced,; ; cf.: rem in eum locum, ut, etc.,: quem in locum,: ergo huc universa causa deducitur, utrum, etc.,: rerum divisio in duos articulos deducitur,: audi, quo rem deducam,what I aim at, what I have in view, to what conclusion I will bring the matter,: Aeolium carmen ad Italos modos,transfer, transplant,; cf.: in patriam deducere musas,. —
In partic.
To mislead, seduce, entice, induce, bring one to an opinion (rare): adolescentibus et oratione magistratus et praemio deductis,; : sibi esse facile, Seuthen regem Thracum deducere, ut, etc.,: aliquem vero,from the truth,.—
To spin out a literary composition, like a thread, i. e. to elaborate, prepare, compose (poet., and in post-Aug. prose): tenui deducta poëmata filo,: mille die versus,; : carmina,; cf. : nihil expositum, : commentarios,: oratio deducta atque circumlata,finely spun out,: primaque ab origine mundi ad mea perpetuum deducite tempora carmen,; cf. ; : opus,. —
(Another figure borrowed from spinning.) To make finer, thinner, weaker; to attenuate: vocem deducas oportet, ut mulieris videantur verba, Pompon. ap. : "Ὀδυσσεύς" ad "Ulixem" deductus est, ; cf. P. a. B.—
To derive (of the origin of words): nomen Christianorum a Christo deducitur,; id. de Virg. vel. 5: diximus nomen religionis a vinculo pietatis esse deductum,; cf.: sed et Pharnacion (cognominatur) a Pharnace rege deductum,.—
To remove, cure, of physical evils: brassica de capite omnia deducet et sanum faciet,: corpore febres, animo curas,; .—
To bring down (late Lat.): deducis ad inferos,i. e. to death,; ; .—
Law t. t., to withhold: cum in mancipanda proprietate (usus fructus) deducatur,.—Hence,

la:verb:dedisco.html:
dē-disco, dĭdĭci, 3,
v. a., to unlearn, to forget, sc. what one has learned (rare, but class.).
With acc.: qui, quod didicit, id dediscit,; cf.: multa oportet discat atque dediscat,; so, haec verba,; cf. : nomen disciplinamque populi Romani, * : sermonem,: cordaque languentem dedidicere metum,: dedidicit jam pace ducem, has unlearned the general, i. e. lost his military character, : dedisce captam,.—Prov.: dediscit animus sero quod didicit diu,.—
With inf.: (eloquentia) loqui dedisceret,; so loqui,: amare,

la:verb:deductus.html:
dēductus, a, um, P. a.
Drawn inwards, bent inwards (only post-Aug.), said of the nose: nasum et a summo eminentiorem et ab imo deductiorem,: nasus deductus,.—
(Acc. to no. II. B. 3.) Slender, weak (ante-class., and once in Verg.): deducta tunc voce leo, with a weak, subdued voice, Lucil. ap. : deducta voce, Afran. and Cornificius ap. : carmen, a humble strain, opp. to canere reges et proelia, (tenue translatio a lana, quae deducitur in tenuitatem, Serv.); cf. also , and .!*? In , deductio, not deducta, is the true reading.

la:verb:deducendus.gloss: which is to be escorted or led away etc.
senses: which is to be escorted or led away etc.

la:verb:dedignor.gloss: to reject as unworthy, disdain, scorn
senses: to reject as unworthy, disdain, scorn
la:verb:dedignor.html:
dē-dignor, ātus, 1,
v. a. dep., to reject as unworthy, to disdain, scorn, refuse (most freq. in Ov.; perh. not ante-Aug.).
With two accs.: quos ego sim toties jam dedignata maritos, * ; so, aliquem maritum,: virum, Pelasgum,: comitem amicum,: Philippum patrem ( = abdicare),: nec dedignanda carmina,.—
With inf.: magni genibus procumbere non est Dedignata Jovis,; ; ; ; —
Absol.: accendebat dedignantes,.

la:verb:dedigno.html:
dē-digno, āvi, 1, v. a., collat. form of dedignor:
tumulos aut ossibus urnas dedignant animae, (Duhn).

la:verb:dedico.html:
dē-dĭco, āvi, ātum, 1 (in the
tmesis: data deque dicata, Lucil. ap. ), v. a., to give out tidings, a notice, etc.; hence, to affirm, declare, announce any thing (cf. de in denuncio and depromo).
In gen. (so only ante- and postclass.): legati quo missi sunt, veniunt, dedicant mandata, Cael. ap. ; Att. ib. (v. 78 Ribbeck); ; cf. ; : aliae (propositiones) dedicativae sunt, quod dedicant aliquid de quopiam; ut: Virtus bonum est: dedicat enim virtuti inesse bonitatem,affirms,; cf. dedicativus.—
Esp.
Relig. t. t., to dedicate, consecrate, set apart a thing to a deity or deified person (for syn. cf.: 1. dico, consecro, inauguro, initio.—Class.): nonne ab A. Postumio aedem Castori ac Polluci in foro dedicatam vides?: aedem Saturno,: aedem Mercurii, et saep.: delubrum Homeri,: simulacrum Jovis,: loca sacris faciendis,: aram Augusto,: domum Dei,; .
With the deity as object instead of the temple: ut Fides, ut Mens, quas in Capitolio dedicatas videmus (i. e. quarum aedes),; (cf. however, ): Junonem,: Apollinem,; and even te quoque magnificā, Concordia, dedicat aede, Livia,.—
Transf. (post-Aug.)
To dedicate, inscribe a composition to any one (for which mittere ad aliquem, or mittere alicui, ; ; ; ): Honori et meritis dedicans illum librum tuis, prol. 30; praef. § 12: perfecto operis tibi dedicati tertio libro, —
In gen., to destine, dispose, prepare, set up a thing for any purpose; to dedicate, consecrate it to any object: equi (sc. Bucephalae) memoriae ac nomini dedicans urbem,: qui proprie libros huic operi dedicaverunt,; ; : Parrhasii tabulam ... in cubiculo dedicavit,: testamentum,to establish,.—
To dedicate, consecrate, devote a thing to its future use: domum,: theatrum,; cf. : amphitheatrum,: thermas atque gymnasium,.—
Law t. t., to specify one's property in the census (rare): tu in uno scorto majorem pecuniam absumsisti, quam quanti omne instrumentum fundi Sabini in censum dedicavisti, P. Afric. ap. ; cf.: at haec praedia in censu (al. censum) dedicavisti? ... Illud quaero sintne ista praedia censui censendo?: omnes in censu villas inde dedicamus aedes, Müll. (dub.).

la:verb:dedoceo.gloss: to cause someone to unlearn something; unteach; teach the opposite of
senses: to cause someone to unlearn something; unteach; teach the opposite of
la:verb:dedoceo.html:
dē-dŏcĕo, ēre,
v. a., to cause one to unlearn something, to unteach, teach the opposite of (rare, but class.).
With double acc.: aliquem geometriam,: regnorum gaudia temet,.—*
With acc. pers. and inf.: (virtus) populum falsis Dedocet uti Vocibus,.—
Pass.: cum aut docendus is est aut dedocendus,: cum a Zenone fortis esse didicisset, a dolore dedoctus est,. In the gerund absol.: onus dedocendi gravius quam docendi,: ut coercendi magis quam dedocendi esse videantur,.

la:noun:dedicatio.html:
dēdĭcātĭo, ōnis, f.
dedico
,
dedication, consecration: aedis,: theatri,; : pontis,: domus Dei, Esdr. 6, 16: statuae,

la:verb:dedecoro.html:
dē-dĕcŏro, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to disgrace, dishonor, bring to shame (class.): mores, quibus boni se dedecorant,: me flagitiis suis,; cf.: se flagitiis,; * ; : et urbis auctoritatem et magistri,; ; (where others read indecorant).

la:adj:dedux.html:
dēdux, ŭcis, adj.
id.
.

= conditor, on a coin ap. Eckhel. IV. p. 347.

la:verb:dedecet.gloss: to be unseemly or unsuitable; to be unbecoming
senses: to be unseemly or unsuitable; to be unbecoming
la:verb:dedecet.html:
dē-dĕcet, cuit, 2,
v. impers. (very rarely pers., v.infra, II.), it is unseemly, unsuitable, unbecoming: decere quasi aptum esse consentaneumque tempori et personae, etc.... contraque item dedecere,.—
Prop. (class.; usually connected with a negation), construed like decet (q. v.), with nom. or inf. rei, and with acc. pers. or absol.
Neque te ministrum dedecet myrtus neque me sub arta vite bibentem, : me usus precum,: nihil se,. In plur.: nec dominam motae dedecuere comae,; .—
Ut, si quid dedeceat, vitemus, : vox,.—
Oratorem irasci minime decet, simulare non dedecet, ; : togam removeri,.—
(Togae) extremam oram rejecisse non dedecet, ; .—
Ut iis, quae habent, modice et scienter utantur, et ut ne dedeceat, . —
By poet. license person. as a v. a., to dishonor, neglect a thing: si non dedecui tua jussa,: Atticus Claudiorum imagines dedecere videbatur,.

la:verb:dedisco#2.html:
dē-disco, dĭdĭci, 3,
v. a., to unlearn, to forget, sc. what one has learned (rare, but class.).
With acc.: qui, quod didicit, id dediscit,; cf.: multa oportet discat atque dediscat,; so, haec verba,; cf. : nomen disciplinamque populi Romani, * : sermonem,: cordaque languentem dedidicere metum,: dedidicit jam pace ducem, has unlearned the general, i. e. lost his military character, : dedisce captam,.—Prov.: dediscit animus sero quod didicit diu,.—

la:noun:deductio.gloss: drawing, draining or leading off or forth
senses: drawing, draining or leading off or forth
la:noun:deductio.html:
dēductĭo, ōnis, f.
deduco
,
a leading away, leading on, in accordance with the different acceptations of the primitive word.
Lit.
In gen.: rivorum a fonte, a leading or conducting off, ; cf.: Albanae aquae,—
In partic.
A leading forth, transplanting of colonies, a colonizing: quae erit in istos agros deductio?; : militum in oppida,: oppidorum,.—
A leading away of the bride: sponsae in domum mariti,.—
An escorting, a conducting safely, .—
A putting out of possession, ejection, expulsion: ibi tum Caecinam postulasse, ut moribus deductio fieret,. —
A deduction, diminution, ; : HERES SINE DEDVCTIONE XX., i. e. vicesimarum,; cf. vicesimus. So, sine deductione,without deduction,; .—
Trop.: ex hac deductione rationis,from this course of reasoning,.

la:noun:deditio.html:
dēdĭtĭo, ōnis, f.

a (military) giving up, a surrender, capitulation (freq. in the historians).—With subj. gen.: deditio sui,.— Plur.: deditiones cohortium,. —With gen. obj.: ipsius corporis,; ; but usually absol.: Helvetii legatos de deditione ad eum miserunt,; cf.: de deditione agere,; : aliquem in deditionem petere,: aliquem in deditionem accipere,; ; ; et saep.: seque in deditionem ut recipiat,: in deditionem redigere,: deditionis condicio,: deditione facta,: subire deditionem,: in deditionem venire,to surrender,; ; : omissa deditione,; cf. An unusual combination is deditionem suam ad aliquem absentem mittere, ; v. Graev. ad loc.
